Useful findings before I ask you a few decisions:

- **Node 23.11 / npm 10.9** available; `node:sqlite` is built-in but experimental → I'd use `better-sqlite3` for stability.
- **Docker CLI is installed but the daemon isn't running** (Docker Desktop not started). Containerization is fine to build; you'll need to start Docker Desktop to verify locally.
- **Ollama is not installed**, and on macOS a containerized Ollama runs CPU-only (no Metal passthrough) → slower. Native Ollama would be GPU-accelerated. This affects how I wire the AI feature.
- 57 GB free disk (llama3.2:3b ≈ 2 GB), arm64.

questions.question: Which stack should I build this in?

options.label: TypeScript end-to-end (Recommended)
options.description: npm workspaces monorepo: React 18 + Vite + TS (web), Node + Express 5 + better-sqlite3 + Zod (api), shared types/schemas package. One language across the stack, strongest type-safety story from DB row → API → UI, and the fastest path to the tests + Docker setup you asked for.

AlertSystem/
├─ apps/api      Express 5 · better-sqlite3 · Zod
├─ apps/web      React 18 · Vite · TS
├─ packages/shared   types + zod schemas (FE+BE)
├─ docker-compose.yml  (api · web · ollama[profile])
└─ Makefile

options.label: Python FastAPI + React
options.description: FastAPI + SQLModel/SQLAlchemy + Pydantic backend, React + TS frontend. Great typing and auto OpenAPI docs, but two languages, two toolchains, two test runners — more setup, and 'full stack language' points away from it.

options.label: TypeScript, single service
options.description: One Node service that serves both the API and the built React bundle — simplest deploy and one container, but weaker separation and a less interesting containerization story.

questions.question: How should the local llama model be wired in?

options.label: Ollama optional profile + deterministic fallback (Recommended)
options.description: Pluggable provider interface. `docker compose up` runs instantly with a deterministic rule-based engine (no 2GB download). `docker compose --profile ai up` adds an ollama container with llama3.2:3b. OLLAMA_BASE_URL also points at a native host Ollama (host.docker.internal) for GPU speed. Reviewer can run it either way; nothing breaks if the model is absent.

options.label: Mocked model interface only
options.description: No real model; a deterministic mock behind the same interface. Fully reproducible and zero setup, but ignores your explicit ask for a real open llama model.

questions.question: Which extras are worth the time? (pick any)

options.label: Playwright E2E + responsive screenshots
options.description: Happy-path E2E (filter → open alert → change status → add note → generate AI insight) plus automated layout checks at 1280/1024/768/375 asserting no text overlap/overflow — directly targets your 'no overlap between containers' requirement.

options.label: AI evaluation harness
options.description: A golden set of ~20 labelled alerts + an offline script scoring schema-validity, groundedness (no invented numbers/sites), and priority agreement vs. the deterministic rules. This is the concrete answer to 'how would you check the output' and is the strongest responsible-AI signal.

options.label: GitHub Actions CI
options.description: Runs lint + typecheck + unit/integration tests and builds the Docker images on push. Cheap to add, shows engineering discipline.

input.content:
# Renewable Operations Incident Board — Implementation Plan

## Context

Take-home assignment. An operations team monitors a portfolio of solar and battery
(BESS) sites. They receive alerts but have no way to answer three questions quickly:

1. **What needs attention right now?** — a flat list sorted by severity is not enough.
   A `critical` alert already being worked matters less than a `high` alert that has sat
   unacknowledged for six hours on a 48 MW site.
2. **What happened?** — the raw alert record is terse and assumes domain knowledge.
3. **What did we do about it?** — follow-up must be recorded and auditable.

The deliverable is a small full-stack web app plus a repository that will be assessed on
**product judgement, usability, software structure, testing, communication, and responsible
use of AI**. The build target is a repo that a reviewer can clone and run in three commands,
with an honest account of what the AI feature can and cannot do.

`/Users/qingfengrumeng/Desktop/AlertSystem` is currently **empty** — this is greenfield.

### Decisions already made (confirmed with user)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Stack | TypeScript end-to-end — npm workspaces monorepo |
| AI runtime | **Native Ollama on the host** (`llama3.2:3b`), primary documented path |
| Persistence | SQLite (`better-sqlite3`) |
| Runtime validation | **Zod everywhere** — env, requests, DB row hydration, AI output, frontend response parsing |
| Extras | Playwright E2E + responsive screenshots, AI eval harness, GitHub Actions CI, deployment config |

### Environment facts verified

- Node v23.11.0, npm 10.9.2, arm64 macOS, 57 GB free.
- **Docker CLI installed but daemon is not running** — user must start Docker Desktop to verify containers.
- **Ollama is not installed** — prerequisite step: `brew install ollama` (Homebrew 6.0.15 present),
  `ollama serve`, `ollama pull llama3.2:3b`.
- Session transcript for `AI_USAGE.md` lives at `~/.claude/projects/-Users-qingfengrumeng-Desktop-AlertSystem/*.jsonl`.

### One noted trade-off on the AI runtime

Native Ollama is the chosen and documented AI path. A deterministic **rule-based engine is still
built**, but *not* as an alternative product — it serves three necessary engineering roles:
(a) the fallback when the model is unreachable/times out/returns invalid output, so the app never
500s; (b) the **baseline the model is cross-checked against** (priority disagreement detection);
(c) the deterministic substrate that makes tests and CI possible without a 2 GB model download.
The README will state plainly that the real AI feature requires Ollama running.

---

## Target architecture

```
AlertSystem/
├─ apps/
│  ├─ api/                     Express 5 · better-sqlite3 · Zod · Vitest
│  └─ web/                     React 18 · Vite · TypeScript · CSS Modules + design tokens
├─ packages/shared/            Zod schemas → z.infer types, shared by API + web
├─ eval/                       AI evaluation harness + labelled golden set
├─ e2e/                        Playwright specs (incl. responsive overflow/overlap audit)
├─ docker/                     Dockerfile.api · Dockerfile.web · nginx.conf
├─ .github/workflows/ci.yml
├─ docker-compose.yml · docker-compose.dev.yml · Makefile
└─ README.md · AI_USAGE.md · IMPROVEMENTS.md
```

**Layering (API):** `routes → services → repositories → db`. Routes only parse/validate and
shape HTTP; domain logic (`triage`, `transitions`, `playbooks`) is **pure and framework-free**
so it is trivially unit-testable and reusable. `app.ts` is an app *factory* returning an Express
app without calling `listen`, so supertest drives it directly.

**Zod as the single source of truth.** `packages/shared` defines the schemas; both sides import
them and derive types with `z.infer`. Validation boundaries:

| Boundary | Schema | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| Process env | `EnvSchema` | fail fast at boot with readable message |
| Request query/params/body | `AlertListQuerySchema`, `PatchAlertSchema`, `CreateNoteSchema` | `400` + field-level `details` |
| DB row → domain object | `AlertRowSchema` (parses `metrics` JSON column, coerces ints→enums/dates) | `500` + log; catches schema drift after migrations |
| LLM output | `InsightSchema` | one repair retry, then rule-based fallback |
| API response → React state | same schemas, re-parsed client-side | surfaced error banner, not a blank screen |

That last row is the one people skip; parsing on the client means a backend contract change
produces a loud, located error instead of `undefined is not an object` three components deep.

---

## Product design

### Triage model — the core product judgement

Severity alone does not rank work. The API computes a **priority** on every read:

```
score = severity_weight × type_multiplier × site_factor
        + age_escalation            (only while new/acknowledged, capped)
        − status_damping            (in_progress ×0.6; resolved/dismissed ⇒ excluded)

severity_weight   critical 100 · high 60 · medium 30 · low 10
type_multiplier   safety 1.5 (thermal runaway, smoke, ground/arc fault)
                  production-loss 1.2 · data-quality 0.8 · informational 0.6
site_factor       1.0 + 0.3 × (capacity_mw / portfolio_max_mw)
bands             P1 ≥ 120 · P2 ≥ 70 · P3 ≥ 35 · P4 otherwise
```

Crucially it returns **`reasons: string[]`** — e.g. `["Critical severity", "Safety-related
type", "Unacknowledged for 6h", "Large site (48 MW)"]` — rendered in a popover. An ops tool
whose ranking cannot be explained will not be trusted.

**"Needs attention"** is a crisp, defensible rule: `status ∈ {new, acknowledged}` **and**
(`priority ∈ {P1, P2}` **or** SLA breached). SLA to acknowledge: P1 15 min · P2 1 h · P3 8 h ·
P4 72 h. Breaches get their own badge and KPI.

The clock is **injected** (`now: Date`) into the scoring function, so tests are deterministic
and seeded data can be generated relative to a fixed instant.

### Data model

- **sites** — `id, name, kind(solar|battery|hybrid), capacity_mw, energy_mwh?, region, timezone`
- **alerts** — `id, site_id, asset_id, type, severity, status, title, description, metrics(JSON),
  detected_at, updated_at, version, source`
- **alert_notes** — `id, alert_id, author, body, created_at`
- **alert_events** — audit trail: `id, alert_id, kind(status_change|note_added|insight_generated),
  from_status, to_status, actor, payload(JSON), created_at`
- **ai_insights** — cache + provenance: `alert_id, provider, model, prompt_hash, content_hash,
  payload(JSON), warnings(JSON), degraded, latency_ms, generated_at`
- **insight_feedback** — `insight_id, helpful, comment, created_at` (human-in-the-loop signal)

`alert_events` is what turns "change a status" into a real audit trail, and `ai_insights` carries
model + timestamp + prompt hash so any displayed AI text is attributable and reproducible.

### Seed data — 18 alerts across 6 sites

Sites: Mojave Ridge Solar (48 MW, CA) · Kestrel Flats BESS (50 MW/100 MWh, AZ) · Harrow Point
Hybrid (35 MW + 12 MW, NSW) · Larkspur BESS (20 MW/80 MWh, TX) · Ellesmere Fields Solar (22 MW, UK)
· Talbot Moor Solar (9.5 MW, UK).

Alert types cover the realistic spread: `inverter_fault`, `inverter_offline`,
`string_underperformance`, `comms_loss`, `battery_cell_temp_high`, `thermal_runaway_risk`,
`bms_fault`, `soc_deviation`, `hvac_failure`, `ground_fault`, `dc_arc_fault`,
`tracker_stow_failure`, `transformer_temp_high`, `ac_breaker_trip`, `grid_voltage_excursion`,
`curtailment`, `irradiance_sensor_fault`, `meter_data_gap`, `soiling_loss`, `aux_power_loss`.

Every alert carries a `metrics` object with real numbers
(`{"cell_temp_c": 58.4, "threshold_c": 55.0, "rack": "R04", "module": "M12"}`). This matters twice:
it gives the model something concrete to ground on, and it gives the groundedness checker a
whitelist of legitimate figures. Deliberate coverage of the awkward cases: one already-resolved,
one dismissed false-positive, one long multi-note history, one with a very long single-token asset
ID, one 4-day-old low-severity item, one whose description contains a prompt-injection string.

Seeding is idempotent (only seeds an empty DB; `--force` resets) and accepts an injected `now`.

### API

Consistent error envelope: `{ error: { code, message, details?, requestId } }`.

| Method | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/health` | db status + `ai: {provider, model, reachable, latencyMs}` |
| GET | `/api/sites` | |
| GET | `/api/alerts` | filters `status[] severity[] siteId[] type[] q from to needsAttention`; `sort=priority\|detectedAt\|severity\|site\|status`; `page/pageSize` (default 25, max 100); returns `{items, total, page, pageSize, facets}` |
| GET | `/api/alerts/:id` | alert + site + notes + events + cached insight |
| PATCH | `/api/alerts/:id` | `{status?, assignee?, expectedVersion}` — `409` stale, `422` illegal transition |
| POST | `/api/alerts/:id/notes` | `{body, author}` |
| POST | `/api/alerts/:id/insight` | `?refresh=true` regenerates; otherwise cached |
| POST | `/api/alerts/:id/insight/feedback` | `{helpful, comment?}` |
| GET | `/api/stats` | KPI strip: needs-attention, open by severity, SLA breaches, resolved 24 h, MTTA |

Status transitions are governed by an explicit matrix (`domain/transitions.ts`) — reopen
(`resolved → in_progress`) is allowed, `dismissed → *` requires reopen, illegal moves are `422`
with the legal set in `details`.

### AI feature — summary · priority · next actions

Provider interface (`ai/types.ts`):

```ts
interface InsightProvider {
  readonly name: string
  isAvailable(): Promise<boolean>
  generate(ctx: AlertContext, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<unknown>  // unknown → Zod parses
}
```

`OllamaProvider` calls `POST {OLLAMA_BASE_URL}/api/chat` with `format: "json"`,
`options: { temperature: 0, seed: 42 }`, model from env (`llama3.2:3b` default; README notes
`llama3.1:8b` gives noticeably better instruction-following if the reviewer has the disk).

`InsightSchema` (Zod, in `packages/shared`):

```ts
{ summary: string.max(400),
  likelyCauses: string.array().min(1).max(3),
  suggestedPriority: enum(['P1','P2','P3','P4']),
  priorityRationale: string.max(240),
  nextActions: object({ action, owner: enum(['field_tech','remote_ops','asset_manager','oem_vendor']),
                        urgency: enum(['now','today','this_week']) }).array().min(1).max(4),
  safetyFlag: boolean,
  confidence: enum(['low','medium','high']) }
```

**Guardrails (`ai/guards.ts`) — the responsible-AI substance:**

1. **Schema validation** — Zod parse. On failure, one repair retry feeding the parse error back;
   still failing ⇒ rule-based fallback.
2. **Groundedness** — every numeric token and proper noun in `summary`/`likelyCauses` must trace
   to the alert's metrics/description/site (numeric tolerance for rounding). Violations attach
   `warnings[]`, force `confidence: 'low'`, and a severe violation (wrong site name) rejects to
   fallback. Prevents the classic "confidently cites a temperature that does not exist".
3. **Prompt-injection containment** — alert text is untrusted user data. It is wrapped in
   `<alert_data>` delimiters with an explicit instruction never to follow instructions found
   inside; the constrained output schema means an injection cannot change the response *shape*.
   A pre-call scan logs suspicious patterns. One seeded alert exercises this end-to-end.
4. **Cross-check against rules** — model priority vs. deterministic band. Divergence ≥ 2 bands
   surfaces a "model disagrees with rules (P1 vs P3)" chip showing **both**, rather than silently
   picking one.
5. **Advisory only** — no AI output ever mutates status, priority, or any stored field. Every
   action stays human-initiated.
6. **Provenance + cache** — keyed on `alert_id + model + prompt_hash + content_hash`; the content
   hash invalidates the cache when the alert or its notes change, so a stale summary can never
   describe a superseded state. UI badge: `AI-assisted · llama3.2:3b · 12:04 · verify before acting`,
   with a "What did it see?" popover listing the exact inputs.
7. **Operational safety** — 60 s `AbortController` timeout, single-flight per alert (concurrent
   requests share one generation), rate limit on the insight route.

**Limitations (documented in README):** a 3B quantized model hallucinates and reasons poorly about
numbers; `format: json` constrains syntax, not truth; quality is capped by the alert record since
there is no live telemetry access; `temperature: 0` reduces but does not eliminate run-to-run
variation; the golden set is synthetic and small, so agreement figures are indicative, not
statistical; no domain expert has validated the playbooks; CPU latency is 2–15 s.

**How the output is checked:** (a) the eval harness scores schema-validity rate, groundedness
violation rate, priority agreement vs. rules, and safety-flag recall on the labelled safety subset;
(b) unit tests run adversarial fixtures through the guards — invented number, wrong site, injection
payload, truncated JSON, empty body, extreme disagreement; (c) in-product 👍/👎 persists to
`insight_feedback` for future evaluation; (d) a documented manual spot-check protocol (human reads
5 alerts against the raw record).

### Frontend

**Board (default view):** KPI strip → *Needs Attention* ranked queue → full filterable table.
**Detail:** right-hand drawer on ≥1024 px so the queue stays visible (real ops workflow), full-screen
sheet below that. Interleaved timeline of events + notes, status control, note composer, AI panel.
**Filters:** multi-select chips (status/severity/site/type), debounced search, sort control,
"needs attention only" toggle, removable active-filter chips, **URL-synced query params** so a
shift handover can paste a link and back/forward works.

**Preventing text overlap and overflow — explicit techniques, not hope:**

- App shell is CSS Grid `grid-template-rows: auto auto minmax(0, 1fr)`; content panes own their
  scroll. No absolutely-positioned text anywhere.
- **`min-width: 0` on every flex/grid child containing text** — this is the actual cause of text
  escaping its container in flex layouts.
- `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on descriptions/notes so a 60-char asset ID cannot push a column;
  `-webkit-line-clamp` for list previews with the full text on `title` and in the drawer.
- Table lives in an `overflow-x: auto` container; below 768 px it becomes a card list rather than
  a crushed table.
- Badges/chips are `inline-flex` with their own padding — they grow, they do not overlap.
- Tokens in `tokens.css` (spacing scale, radii, AA-contrast severity/status colours in light + dark,
  `prefers-reduced-motion`). Severity is conveyed by **icon + text + colour**, never colour alone.
- Drawer: focus trap, Esc to close, focus returns to the originating row, `aria-modal`.
- Every async surface has loading (skeleton) / error (retry) / empty (with "clear filters") states.

This is then **verified automatically**, not just asserted — see the Playwright layout audit below.

---

## Edge cases explicitly handled

**API/data:** illegal status transition (`422` + legal set) · concurrent edit via `expectedVersion`
(`409`) · whitespace-only or oversized note (`400`) · unknown id (`404`) · invalid/negative/huge
query params (`400`, pageSize clamped) · zero-result filter combination (empty state + clear action)
· stable sort tie-break by id so pagination cannot duplicate or skip rows · all timestamps stored
UTC ISO-8601, displayed site-local + relative, future-dated (clock skew) rendered as "just now" ·
parameterised statements only · WAL + `busy_timeout` for concurrent writers · migrations idempotent
at boot.

**AI:** Ollama not running / model not pulled / partial download · request timeout and stalled
stream · malformed or truncated JSON · hallucinated numbers, sites, or asset IDs · prompt injection
in description or notes · very long note history (most-recent-N within a token budget) · duplicate
concurrent generate requests · non-ASCII/emoji in alert text.

**UI:** long unbroken tokens · very long descriptions · 375 px viewport · empty portfolio · all
alerts resolved · a site with zero alerts · keyboard-only navigation · double-submit of status
change (button disabled while in flight, request idempotent via `expectedVersion`).

---

## Task breakdown

Each task is plan → code → test. Estimates are rough working time.

### T0 · Scaffold and tooling (~30 m)
`git init`; npm workspaces root; TypeScript project references; ESLint + Prettier; Vitest config;
`packages/shared` with the first Zod schemas (enums for severity/status/type/priority); `.env.example`;
`Makefile`; `.gitignore`. **Check:** `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass on an empty suite.

### T1 · Data layer (~45 m)
`db/client.ts` (WAL, `busy_timeout`, foreign keys on), `migrations/001_init.sql`, `migrate.ts` with a
`schema_migrations` table, `seed.ts` (18 alerts, injected clock, idempotent, `--force`), repositories
with **Zod row-hydration schemas**. **Test:** migrations run twice cleanly; seed is idempotent; a
corrupted `metrics` JSON column fails loudly at hydration.

### T2 · Triage engine (~30 m)
Pure `domain/triage.ts`, `domain/transitions.ts`, `domain/playbooks.ts`. **Test:** band boundaries,
age-escalation cap, status damping, safety multiplier, `reasons` content, SLA breach detection, full
transition matrix, determinism under a fixed clock.

### T3 · REST API (~60 m)
App factory, Zod validation middleware, error envelope + request id, routes, `/api/stats`, rate limit.
**Test (supertest, fresh temp SQLite per file):** filtering/sorting/pagination incl. tie-break, `400`
on bad params, `404`, `422` illegal transition, `409` stale version, note validation, audit-event
writes, injection-shaped query strings.

### T4 · AI insight service (~75 m)
Provider interface, `OllamaProvider`, `RuleBasedProvider`, prompt builder with data delimiting,
`InsightSchema`, `guards.ts`, caching + single-flight + content-hash invalidation, feedback endpoint.
**Test:** stubbed-OK path caches on second call; unreachable Ollama returns `200` + `degraded: true`
and never `500`; malformed JSON triggers repair-then-fallback; each guard has an adversarial fixture.
Plus one manual run against real Ollama.

### T5 · Frontend (~2 h)
Design tokens and app shell; API client that **re-parses responses with the shared Zod schemas**;
KPI strip; needs-attention queue; filter bar with URL sync; alert table/card list; detail drawer with
status control, note composer, timeline; AI panel with provenance badge, disagreement chip, warnings,
and 👍/👎. **Test (RTL):** URL↔filter sync, drawer keyboard behaviour, AI panel provenance and
degraded states, clamped text stays within bounds.

### T6 · E2E, evaluation harness, CI (~75 m)
Playwright happy path (filter → open → status → note → generate insight) with Ollama intercepted for
CI determinism plus a `@live` variant against real Ollama. **Layout audit spec:** at 1280/1024/768/375,
assert every text node satisfies `scrollWidth ≤ clientWidth + 1` and that sibling container bounding
boxes do not intersect — this mechanises the "no overlap between containers of text" requirement.
axe-core scan with zero serious/critical violations. Screenshots to `docs/screenshots/`.

   A `critical` alert already being worked matters less than a `high` alert that has sat
   unacknowledged for six hours on a 48 MW site.
2. **What happened?** — the raw alert record is terse and assumes domain knowledge.
3. **What did we do about it?** — follow-up must be recorded and auditable.

The deliverable is a small full-stack web app plus a repository that will be assessed on
**product judgement, usability, software structure, testing, communication, and responsible
use of AI**. The build target is a repo that a reviewer can clone and run in three commands,
with an honest account of what the AI feature can and cannot do.

`/Users/qingfengrumeng/Desktop/AlertSystem` is currently **empty** — this is greenfield.

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Stack | TypeScript end-to-end — npm workspaces monorepo |
| AI runtime | **Native Ollama on the host** (`llama3.2:3b`), primary documented path |
| Persistence | SQLite (`better-sqlite3`) |
| Runtime validation | **Zod everywhere** — env, requests, DB row hydration, AI output, frontend response parsing |
| Extras | Playwright E2E + responsive screenshots, AI eval harness, GitHub Actions CI, deployment config |

### Environment facts verified

- Node v23.11.0, npm 10.9.2, arm64 macOS, 57 GB free.
- **Docker CLI installed but daemon is not running** — user must start Docker Desktop to verify containers.
- **Ollama is not installed** — prerequisite step: `brew install ollama` (Homebrew 6.0.15 present),

- Session transcript for `AI_USAGE.md` lives at `~/.claude/projects/-Users-qingfengrumeng-Desktop-AlertSystem/*.jsonl`.

### One noted trade-off on the AI runtime

Native Ollama is the chosen and documented AI path. A deterministic **rule-based engine is still
built**, but *not* as an alternative product — it serves three necessary engineering roles:
(a) the fallback when the model is unreachable/times out/returns invalid output, so the app never
500s; (b) the **baseline the model is cross-checked against** (priority disagreement detection);
(c) the deterministic substrate that makes tests and CI possible without a 2 GB model download.
The README will state plainly that the real AI feature requires Ollama running.

---

## Target architecture

```
AlertSystem/
├─ apps/
│  ├─ api/                     Express 5 · better-sqlite3 · Zod · Vitest
│  └─ web/                     React 18 · Vite · TypeScript · CSS Modules + design tokens
├─ packages/shared/            Zod schemas → z.infer types, shared by API + web
├─ eval/                       AI evaluation harness + labelled golden set
├─ e2e/                        Playwright specs (incl. responsive overflow/overlap audit)
├─ docker/                     Dockerfile.api · Dockerfile.web · nginx.conf
├─ .github/workflows/ci.yml
├─ docker-compose.yml · docker-compose.dev.yml · Makefile
└─ README.md · AI_USAGE.md · IMPROVEMENTS.md
```

**Layering (API):** `routes → services → repositories → db`. Routes only parse/validate and
shape HTTP; domain logic (`triage`, `transitions`, `playbooks`) is **pure and framework-free**
so it is trivially unit-testable and reusable. `app.ts` is an app *factory* returning an Express
app without calling `listen`, so supertest drives it directly.

**Zod as the single source of truth.** `packages/shared` defines the schemas; both sides import
them and derive types with `z.infer`. Validation boundaries:

| Boundary | Schema | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| Process env | `EnvSchema` | fail fast at boot with readable message |
| Request query/params/body | `AlertListQuerySchema`, `PatchAlertSchema`, `CreateNoteSchema` | `400` + field-level `details` |
| DB row → domain object | `AlertRowSchema` (parses `metrics` JSON column, coerces ints→enums/dates) | `500` + log; catches schema drift after migrations |
| LLM output | `InsightSchema` | one repair retry, then rule-based fallback |
| API response → React state | same schemas, re-parsed client-side | surfaced error banner, not a blank screen |

That last row is the one people skip; parsing on the client means a backend contract change
produces a loud, located error instead of `undefined is not an object` three components deep.

## Product design

### Triage model — the core product judgement

Severity alone does not rank work. The API computes a **priority** on every read:

```
score = severity_weight × type_multiplier × site_factor
        + age_escalation            (only while new/acknowledged, capped)
        − status_damping            (in_progress ×0.6; resolved/dismissed ⇒ excluded)

severity_weight   critical 100 · high 60 · medium 30 · low 10
type_multiplier   safety 1.5 (thermal runaway, smoke, ground/arc fault)
                  production-loss 1.2 · data-quality 0.8 · informational 0.6
site_factor       1.0 + 0.3 × (capacity_mw / portfolio_max_mw)
bands             P1 ≥ 120 · P2 ≥ 70 · P3 ≥ 35 · P4 otherwise
```

Crucially it returns **`reasons: string[]`** — e.g. `["Critical severity", "Safety-related
type", "Unacknowledged for 6h", "Large site (48 MW)"]` — rendered in a popover. An ops tool
whose ranking cannot be explained will not be trusted.

**"Needs attention"** is a crisp, defensible rule: `status ∈ {new, acknowledged}` **and**
(`priority ∈ {P1, P2}` **or** SLA breached). SLA to acknowledge: P1 15 min · P2 1 h · P3 8 h ·
P4 72 h. Breaches get their own badge and KPI.

and seeded data can be generated relative to a fixed instant.

- **sites** — `id, name, kind(solar|battery|hybrid), capacity_mw, energy_mwh?, region, timezone`
- **alerts** — `id, site_id, asset_id, type, severity, status, title, description, metrics(JSON),
  detected_at, updated_at, version, source`
- **alert_notes** — `id, alert_id, author, body, created_at`
- **alert_events** — audit trail: `id, alert_id, kind(status_change|note_added|insight_generated),
  from_status, to_status, actor, payload(JSON), created_at`
- **ai_insights** — cache + provenance: `alert_id, provider, model, prompt_hash, content_hash,
  payload(JSON), warnings(JSON), degraded, latency_ms, generated_at`
- **insight_feedback** — `insight_id, helpful, comment, created_at` (human-in-the-loop signal)

`alert_events` is what turns "change a status" into a real audit trail, and `ai_insights` carries
model + timestamp + prompt hash so any displayed AI text is attributable and reproducible.

### Seed data — 18 alerts across 6 sites

Sites: Mojave Ridge Solar (48 MW, CA) · Kestrel Flats BESS (50 MW/100 MWh, AZ) · Harrow Point
Hybrid (35 MW + 12 MW, NSW) · Larkspur BESS (20 MW/80 MWh, TX) · Ellesmere Fields Solar (22 MW, UK)
· Talbot Moor Solar (9.5 MW, UK).

Alert types cover the realistic spread: `inverter_fault`, `inverter_offline`,
`string_underperformance`, `comms_loss`, `battery_cell_temp_high`, `thermal_runaway_risk`,
`bms_fault`, `soc_deviation`, `hvac_failure`, `ground_fault`, `dc_arc_fault`,
`tracker_stow_failure`, `transformer_temp_high`, `ac_breaker_trip`, `grid_voltage_excursion`,
`curtailment`, `irradiance_sensor_fault`, `meter_data_gap`, `soiling_loss`, `aux_power_loss`.

Every alert carries a `metrics` object with real numbers
(`{"cell_temp_c": 58.4, "threshold_c": 55.0, "rack": "R04", "module": "M12"}`). This matters twice:
it gives the model something concrete to ground on, and it gives the groundedness checker a
whitelist of legitimate figures. Deliberate coverage of the awkward cases: one already-resolved,
one dismissed false-positive, one long multi-note history, one with a very long single-token asset
ID, one 4-day-old low-severity item, one whose description contains a prompt-injection string.

Seeding is idempotent (only seeds an empty DB; `--force` resets) and accepts an injected `now`.

### API

Consistent error envelope: `{ error: { code, message, details?, requestId } }`.

| Method | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/health` | db status + `ai: {provider, model, reachable, latencyMs}` |
| GET | `/api/sites` | |
| GET | `/api/alerts` | filters `status[] severity[] siteId[] type[] q from to needsAttention`; `sort=priority\|detectedAt\|severity\|site\|status`; `page/pageSize` (default 25, max 100); returns `{items, total, page, pageSize, facets}` |

| PATCH | `/api/alerts/:id` | `{status?, assignee?, expectedVersion}` — `409` stale, `422` illegal transition |
| POST | `/api/alerts/:id/notes` | `{body, author}` |
| POST | `/api/alerts/:id/insight` | `?refresh=true` regenerates; otherwise cached |
| POST | `/api/alerts/:id/insight/feedback` | `{helpful, comment?}` |
| GET | `/api/stats` | KPI strip: needs-attention, open by severity, SLA breaches, resolved 24 h, MTTA |

(`resolved → in_progress`) is allowed, `dismissed → *` requires reopen, illegal moves are `422`
with the legal set in `details`.

Provider interface (`ai/types.ts`):

```ts
interface InsightProvider {
  readonly name: string
  isAvailable(): Promise<boolean>
  generate(ctx: AlertContext, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<unknown>  // unknown → Zod parses
}
```

```ts
{ summary: string.max(400),
  likelyCauses: string.array().min(1).max(3),
  suggestedPriority: enum(['P1','P2','P3','P4']),
  priorityRationale: string.max(240),
  nextActions: object({ action, owner: enum(['field_tech','remote_ops','asset_manager','oem_vendor']),

  safetyFlag: boolean,
  confidence: enum(['low','medium','high']) }
```

1. **Schema validation** — Zod parse. On failure, one repair retry feeding the parse error back;
   still failing ⇒ rule-based fallback.
2. **Groundedness** — every numeric token and proper noun in `summary`/`likelyCauses` must trace

   picking one.
5. **Advisory only** — no AI output ever mutates status, priority, or any stored field. Every
   action stays human-initiated.
6. **Provenance + cache** — keyed on `alert_id + model + prompt_hash + content_hash`; the content
   hash invalidates the cache when the alert or its notes change, so a stale summary can never
   describe a superseded state. UI badge: `AI-assisted · llama3.2:3b · 12:04 · verify before acting`,

- **`min-width: 0` on every flex/grid child containing text** — this is the actual cause of text

- Drawer: focus trap, Esc to close, focus returns to the originating row, `aria-modal`.

```ts

  suggestedPriority: enum(['P1','P2','P3','P4']),
  priorityRationale: string.max(240),
  nextActions: object({ action, owner: enum(['field_tech','remote_ops','asset_manager','oem_vendor']),

  safetyFlag: boolean,

```

**Guardrails (`ai/guards.ts`) — the responsible-AI substance:**

1. **Schema validation** — Zod parse. On failure, one repair retry feeding the parse error back;
   still failing ⇒ rule-based fallback.
2. **Groundedness** — every numeric token and proper noun in `summary`/`likelyCauses` must trace
   to the alert's metrics/description/site (numeric tolerance for rounding). Violations attach

3. **Prompt-injection containment** — alert text is untrusted user data. It is wrapped in
   `<alert_data>` delimiters with an explicit instruction never to follow instructions found
   inside; the constrained output schema means an injection cannot change the response *shape*.
   A pre-call scan logs suspicious patterns. One seeded alert exercises this end-to-end.
4. **Cross-check against rules** — model priority vs. deterministic band. Divergence ≥ 2 bands
   surfaces a "model disagrees with rules (P1 vs P3)" chip showing **both**, rather than silently
   picking one.
5. **Advisory only** — no AI output ever mutates status, priority, or any stored field. Every
   action stays human-initiated.

   describe a superseded state. UI badge: `AI-assisted · llama3.2:3b · 12:04 · verify before acting`,

   requests share one generation), rate limit on the insight route.

numbers; `format: json` constrains syntax, not truth; quality is capped by the alert record since
there is no live telemetry access; `temperature: 0` reduces but does not eliminate run-to-run
variation; the golden set is synthetic and small, so agreement figures are indicative, not
statistical; no domain expert has validated the playbooks; CPU latency is 2–15 s.

**How the output is checked:** (a) the eval harness scores schema-validity rate, groundedness
violation rate, priority agreement vs. rules, and safety-flag recall on the labelled safety subset;
(b) unit tests run adversarial fixtures through the guards — invented number, wrong site, injection
payload, truncated JSON, empty body, extreme disagreement; (c) in-product 👍/👎 persists to
`insight_feedback` for future evaluation; (d) a documented manual spot-check protocol (human reads
5 alerts against the raw record).

## Edge cases explicitly handled

**API/data:** illegal status transition (`422` + legal set) · concurrent edit via `expectedVersion`
(`409`) · whitespace-only or oversized note (`400`) · unknown id (`404`) · invalid/negative/huge
query params (`400`, pageSize clamped) · zero-result filter combination (empty state + clear action)
· stable sort tie-break by id so pagination cannot duplicate or skip rows · all timestamps stored
UTC ISO-8601, displayed site-local + relative, future-dated (clock skew) rendered as "just now" ·
parameterised statements only · WAL + `busy_timeout` for concurrent writers · migrations idempotent
at boot.

**AI:** Ollama not running / model not pulled / partial download · request timeout and stalled
stream · malformed or truncated JSON · hallucinated numbers, sites, or asset IDs · prompt injection
in description or notes · very long note history (most-recent-N within a token budget) · duplicate
concurrent generate requests · non-ASCII/emoji in alert text.

**UI:** long unbroken tokens · very long descriptions · 375 px viewport · empty portfolio · all
alerts resolved · a site with zero alerts · keyboard-only navigation · double-submit of status
change (button disabled while in flight, request idempotent via `expectedVersion`).

(BESS) sites. They receive alerts but have no way to answer three questions quickly:

   A `critical` alert already being worked matters less than a `high` alert that has sat
   unacknowledged for six hours on a 48 MW site.
2. **What happened?** — the raw alert record is terse and assumes domain knowledge.
3. **What did we do about it?** — follow-up must be recorded and auditable.

The deliverable is a small full-stack web app plus a repository that will be assessed on
**product judgement, usability, software structure, testing, communication, and responsible
use of AI**. The build target is a repo that a reviewer can clone and run in three commands,
with an honest account of what the AI feature can and cannot do.

`/Users/qingfengrumeng/Desktop/AlertSystem` is currently **empty** — this is greenfield.

### Decisions already made (confirmed with user)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Stack | TypeScript end-to-end — npm workspaces monorepo |
| AI runtime | **Native Ollama on the host** (`llama3.2:3b`), primary documented path |
| Persistence | SQLite (`better-sqlite3`) |
| Runtime validation | **Zod everywhere** — env, requests, DB row hydration, AI output, frontend response parsing |
| Extras | Playwright E2E + responsive screenshots, AI eval harness, GitHub Actions CI, deployment config |

### Environment facts verified

- Node v23.11.0, npm 10.9.2, arm64 macOS, 57 GB free.
- **Docker CLI installed but daemon is not running** — user must start Docker Desktop to verify containers.
- **Ollama is not installed** — prerequisite step: `brew install ollama` (Homebrew 6.0.15 present),

Native Ollama is the chosen and documented AI path. A deterministic **rule-based engine is still
built**, but *not* as an alternative product — it serves three necessary engineering roles:
(a) the fallback when the model is unreachable/times out/returns invalid output, so the app never

## Target architecture

```
AlertSystem/
├─ apps/
│  ├─ api/                     Express 5 · better-sqlite3 · Zod · Vitest
│  └─ web/                     React 18 · Vite · TypeScript · CSS Modules + design tokens
├─ packages/shared/            Zod schemas → z.infer types, shared by API + web
├─ eval/                       AI evaluation harness + labelled golden set
├─ e2e/                        Playwright specs (incl. responsive overflow/overlap audit)
├─ docker/                     Dockerfile.api · Dockerfile.web · nginx.conf
├─ .github/workflows/ci.yml
├─ docker-compose.yml · docker-compose.dev.yml · Makefile
└─ README.md · AI_USAGE.md · IMPROVEMENTS.md
```

**Layering (API):** `routes → services → repositories → db`. Routes only parse/validate and
shape HTTP; domain logic (`triage`, `transitions`, `playbooks`) is **pure and framework-free**
so it is trivially unit-testable and reusable. `app.ts` is an app *factory* returning an Express

them and derive types with `z.infer`. Validation boundaries:

|---|---|---|

```
        − status_damping            (in_progress ×0.6; resolved/dismissed ⇒ excluded)

type_multiplier   safety 1.5 (thermal runaway, smoke, ground/arc fault)
```

   describe a superseded state. UI badge: `AI-assisted · llama3.2:3b · 12:04 · verify before acting`,
   with a "What did it see?" popover listing the exact inputs.
7. **Operational safety** — 60 s `AbortController` timeout, single-flight per alert (concurrent
   requests share one generation), rate limit on the insight route.

**Limitations (documented in README):** a 3B quantized model hallucinates and reasons poorly about
numbers; `format: json` constrains syntax, not truth; quality is capped by the alert record since
there is no live telemetry access; `temperature: 0` reduces but does not eliminate run-to-run
variation; the golden set is synthetic and small, so agreement figures are indicative, not
statistical; no domain expert has validated the playbooks; CPU latency is 2–15 s.

**How the output is checked:** (a) the eval harness scores schema-validity rate, groundedness
violation rate, priority agreement vs. rules, and safety-flag recall on the labelled safety subset;
(b) unit tests run adversarial fixtures through the guards — invented number, wrong site, injection
payload, truncated JSON, empty body, extreme disagreement; (c) in-product 👍/👎 persists to
`insight_feedback` for future evaluation; (d) a documented manual spot-check protocol (human reads
5 alerts against the raw record).

### Frontend

**Board (default view):** KPI strip → *Needs Attention* ranked queue → full filterable table.
**Detail:** right-hand drawer on ≥1024 px so the queue stays visible (real ops workflow), full-screen
sheet below that. Interleaved timeline of events + notes, status control, note composer, AI panel.
**Filters:** multi-select chips (status/severity/site/type), debounced search, sort control,
"needs attention only" toggle, removable active-filter chips, **URL-synced query params** so a
shift handover can paste a link and back/forward works.

**Preventing text overlap and overflow — explicit techniques, not hope:**

- App shell is CSS Grid `grid-template-rows: auto auto minmax(0, 1fr)`; content panes own their
  scroll. No absolutely-positioned text anywhere.
- **`min-width: 0` on every flex/grid child containing text** — this is the actual cause of text
  escaping its container in flex layouts.
- `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on descriptions/notes so a 60-char asset ID cannot push a column;
  `-webkit-line-clamp` for list previews with the full text on `title` and in the drawer.
- Table lives in an `overflow-x: auto` container; below 768 px it becomes a card list rather than
  a crushed table.
- Badges/chips are `inline-flex` with their own padding — they grow, they do not overlap.
- Tokens in `tokens.css` (spacing scale, radii, AA-contrast severity/status colours in light + dark,
  `prefers-reduced-motion`). Severity is conveyed by **icon + text + colour**, never colour alone.
- Drawer: focus trap, Esc to close, focus returns to the originating row, `aria-modal`.
- Every async surface has loading (skeleton) / error (retry) / empty (with "clear filters") states.

This is then **verified automatically**, not just asserted — see the Playwright layout audit below.

---

## Edge cases explicitly handled

**API/data:** illegal status transition (`422` + legal set) · concurrent edit via `expectedVersion`
(`409`) · whitespace-only or oversized note (`400`) · unknown id (`404`) · invalid/negative/huge
query params (`400`, pageSize clamped) · zero-result filter combination (empty state + clear action)
· stable sort tie-break by id so pagination cannot duplicate or skip rows · all timestamps stored
UTC ISO-8601, displayed site-local + relative, future-dated (clock skew) rendered as "just now" ·
parameterised statements only · WAL + `busy_timeout` for concurrent writers · migrations idempotent
at boot.

**AI:** Ollama not running / model not pulled / partial download · request timeout and stalled
stream · malformed or truncated JSON · hallucinated numbers, sites, or asset IDs · prompt injection
in description or notes · very long note history (most-recent-N within a token budget) · duplicate
concurrent generate requests · non-ASCII/emoji in alert text.

**UI:** long unbroken tokens · very long descriptions · 375 px viewport · empty portfolio · all
alerts resolved · a site with zero alerts · keyboard-only navigation · double-submit of status
change (button disabled while in flight, request idempotent via `expectedVersion`).

---

## Task breakdown

Each task is plan → code → test. Estimates are rough working time.

### T0 · Scaffold and tooling (~30 m)
`git init`; npm workspaces root; TypeScript project references; ESLint + Prettier; Vitest config;
`packages/shared` with the first Zod schemas (enums for severity/status/type/priority); `.env.example`;
`Makefile`; `.gitignore`. **Check:** `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass on an empty suite.

### T1 · Data layer (~45 m)
`db/client.ts` (WAL, `busy_timeout`, foreign keys on), `migrations/001_init.sql`, `migrate.ts` with a
`schema_migrations` table, `seed.ts` (18 alerts, injected clock, idempotent, `--force`), repositories
with **Zod row-hydration schemas**. **Test:** migrations run twice cleanly; seed is idempotent; a
corrupted `metrics` JSON column fails loudly at hydration.

### T2 · Triage engine (~30 m)
Pure `domain/triage.ts`, `domain/transitions.ts`, `domain/playbooks.ts`. **Test:** band boundaries,
age-escalation cap, status damping, safety multiplier, `reasons` content, SLA breach detection, full
transition matrix, determinism under a fixed clock.

### T3 · REST API (~60 m)
App factory, Zod validation middleware, error envelope + request id, routes, `/api/stats`, rate limit.
**Test (supertest, fresh temp SQLite per file):** filtering/sorting/pagination incl. tie-break, `400`
on bad params, `404`, `422` illegal transition, `409` stale version, note validation, audit-event
writes, injection-shaped query strings.

### T4 · AI insight service (~75 m)
Provider interface, `OllamaProvider`, `RuleBasedProvider`, prompt builder with data delimiting,
`InsightSchema`, `guards.ts`, caching + single-flight + content-hash invalidation, feedback endpoint.
**Test:** stubbed-OK path caches on second call; unreachable Ollama returns `200` + `degraded: true`
and never `500`; malformed JSON triggers repair-then-fallback; each guard has an adversarial fixture.
Plus one manual run against real Ollama.

### T5 · Frontend (~2 h)
Design tokens and app shell; API client that **re-parses responses with the shared Zod schemas**;
KPI strip; needs-attention queue; filter bar with URL sync; alert table/card list; detail drawer with
status control, note composer, timeline; AI panel with provenance badge, disagreement chip, warnings,
and 👍/👎. **Test (RTL):** URL↔filter sync, drawer keyboard behaviour, AI panel provenance and
degraded states, clamped text stays within bounds.

### T6 · E2E, evaluation harness, CI (~75 m)
Playwright happy path (filter → open → status → note → generate insight) with Ollama intercepted for
CI determinism plus a `@live` variant against real Ollama. **Layout audit spec:** at 1280/1024/768/375,
assert every text node satisfies `scrollWidth ≤ clientWidth + 1` and that sibling container bounding
boxes do not intersect — this mechanises the "no overlap between containers of text" requirement.
axe-core scan with zero serious/critical violations. Screenshots to `docs/screenshots/`.
`eval/` golden set (~20 labelled alerts) + `npm run eval` printing schema-validity, groundedness,
priority agreement, safety recall. GitHub Actions: lint → typecheck → unit/integration → build →
Playwright (mocked AI) → docker build.

### T7 · Containerization and deployment (~45 m)
`Dockerfile.api` multi-stage (builder with build-essential for `better-sqlite3` → slim runtime,
non-root, `/data` volume, `HEALTHCHECK`); `Dockerfile.web` (vite build → nginx serving static +
`/api` proxy + SPA fallback); `docker-compose.yml` with named volume and
`OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:11434` + `extra_hosts: host-gateway` so the containerised
API reaches **native host Ollama**; an optional `ollama` service behind `--profile ai` for Linux/CI;
`docker-compose.dev.yml` for hot reload; Fly.io `fly.toml` + volume for `/data`.
**Check:** `docker compose up` → app usable at `localhost:8080` with AI live from the host model.
*(Requires the user to start Docker Desktop.)*

### T8 · Documentation (~45 m)
`README.md`: prerequisites (incl. `brew install ollama`, `ollama pull llama3.2:3b`), three-command
quickstart, mermaid architecture diagram, data model, API table, triage model explained, AI feature
with limitations and verification, testing guide, trade-offs, edge-case list.
`AI_USAGE.md`: generated from the session `.jsonl` — verbatim prompts, material assistant outputs,
corrections and iterations, redaction markers where applicable, and a "how I checked the AI's work"
section. `IMPROVEMENTS.md`: what more time would buy. Commits are logical and incremental throughout,
not one dump at the end.

---

## Verification

1. `make dev` → API on 3001, web on 5173; walk the board, open an alert, change status, add a note,
   generate an insight with Ollama running.
2. `npm test` — unit + integration, all green.
3. `npm run e2e` — happy path, responsive layout audit at four widths, axe scan.
4. `npm run eval` — prints the AI quality table; recorded in the README.

6. `docker compose up` → full stack at `localhost:8080` reaching host Ollama.

8. Fresh-clone rehearsal: `git clone && make up` following only the README.

## Open prerequisite for the user

`brew install ollama && ollama serve && ollama pull llama3.2:3b`, and start Docker Desktop before T7.

/**
 * Migrations are TypeScript modules rather than `.sql` files on purpose: `tsc` does not copy
 * non-TS assets into `dist/`, so shipping SQL as data would mean adding a copy step to the
 * build and a matching COPY to the Dockerfile. Keeping them as exported strings means the
 * compiled output and the container image are correct by construction.
 *
 * Each migration is applied exactly once, in id order, inside a transaction.
 */

export interface Migration {
  readonly id: number;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly sql: string;
}

const initial: Migration = {
  id: 1,
  name: 'initial_schema',
  sql: /* sql */ `
    CREATE TABLE sites (
      id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      name          TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
      kind          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('solar', 'battery', 'hybrid')),
      capacity_mw   REAL NOT NULL CHECK (capacity_mw > 0),
      energy_mwh    REAL          CHECK (energy_mwh IS NULL OR energy_mwh > 0),
      region        TEXT NOT NULL,
      timezone      TEXT NOT NULL,
      grid_operator TEXT NOT NULL
    );

    CREATE TABLE alerts (
      id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      site_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES sites(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      asset_id        TEXT,
      -- The set of alert types is enforced by Zod at every write boundary rather than by a
      -- CHECK constraint: adding a type should be a code change, not a schema migration.
      -- The read-side hydration schema still rejects anything unexpected that reaches the
      -- table by another route.
      type            TEXT NOT NULL,
      severity        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (severity IN ('critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low')),
      status          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('new', 'acknowledged', 'in_progress', 'resolved', 'dismissed')),
      title           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(title)) > 0),
      description     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(description)) > 0),
      metrics         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}' CHECK (json_valid(metrics)),
      detected_at     TEXT NOT NULL,
      updated_at      TEXT NOT NULL,
      acknowledged_at TEXT,
      resolved_at     TEXT,
      assignee        TEXT,
      source          TEXT NOT NULL,
      version         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (version >= 0)
    );

    CREATE INDEX idx_alerts_status      ON alerts(status);
    CREATE INDEX idx_alerts_severity    ON alerts(severity);
    CREATE INDEX idx_alerts_site        ON alerts(site_id);
    CREATE INDEX idx_alerts_type        ON alerts(type);
    CREATE INDEX idx_alerts_detected_at ON alerts(detected_at DESC);

    CREATE TABLE alert_notes (
      id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
      alert_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES alerts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      author     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(author)) > 0),
      body       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(body)) > 0),
      created_at TEXT NOT NULL
    );

    CREATE INDEX idx_notes_alert ON alert_notes(alert_id, created_at);

    -- Append-only audit trail. Every status change, note and generated insight lands here,
    -- which is what makes "record follow-up actions" auditable rather than just editable.
    CREATE TABLE alert_events (
      id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
      alert_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES alerts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      kind        TEXT NOT NULL,
      from_status TEXT,
      to_status   TEXT,
      actor       TEXT NOT NULL,
      detail      TEXT,
      created_at  TEXT NOT NULL
    );

    CREATE INDEX idx_events_alert ON alert_events(alert_id, created_at);

    -- Cached model output plus the provenance needed to audit it later.
    CREATE TABLE ai_insights (
      id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
      alert_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES alerts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      provider        TEXT NOT NULL,
      model           TEXT NOT NULL,
      payload         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(payload)),
      degraded        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (degraded IN (0, 1)),
      degraded_reason TEXT,
      warnings        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]' CHECK (json_valid(warnings)),
      rule_baseline   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(rule_baseline)),
      disagreement    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(disagreement)),
      latency_ms      INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (latency_ms >= 0),
      generated_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
      prompt_hash     TEXT NOT NULL,
      -- Hash of the alert content the answer describes. When the alert or its notes change
      -- this no longer matches, so a stale summary can never be served for new facts.
      content_hash    TEXT NOT NULL
    );

    CREATE INDEX idx_insights_alert ON ai_insights(alert_id, generated_at DESC);

    -- Operator verdict on a generated insight. Persisted so the quality of the AI feature can
    -- be measured against real usage instead of guessed at.
    CREATE TABLE insight_feedback (
      id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
      insight_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES ai_insights(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      helpful    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (helpful IN (0, 1)),
      comment    TEXT,
      created_at TEXT NOT NULL
    );

    CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_feedback_insight ON insight_feedback(insight_id);
  `,
};

export const MIGRATIONS: readonly Migration[] = [initial];

import type { Alert, Site } from '@incident-board/shared';

/**
 * Mock portfolio and alert history.
 *
 * Everything is generated relative to an injected `now` so the board always looks live, while
 * tests can pin the clock and get byte-identical output. Several rows exist specifically to
 * exercise awkward paths rather than to look good in a screenshot:
 *
 *  - `ALT-1035` carries a prompt-injection string in its description.
 *  - `ALT-1032` has a 55-character unbroken asset id, to prove the layout truncates instead of
 *    overflowing its column.
 *  - `ALT-1030` is a four-day-old low-severity alert whose SLA has blown: it should show a
 *    breach badge but must *not* enter the act-now queue.
 *  - `ALT-1037` is resolved and `ALT-1027` was dismissed as a false positive, so closed states
 *    are represented.
 *  - `ALT-1039` has a multi-note history, so the timeline is not always empty.
 */

export interface SeedNote {
  alertId: string;
  author: string;
  body: string;
  /** Minutes after the alert was detected, so notes stay ordered relative to their alert. */
  minutesAfterDetection: number;
}

  notes: SeedNote[];
}

export function buildSeedData(now: Date): SeedData {
  const at = (hoursAgo: number): string =>
    new Date(now.getTime() - hoursAgo * 3_600_000).toISOString();

  const alerts: Alert[] = ALERT_SEEDS.map((seed) => {
    // `updated_at` is the most recent thing that happened to the alert, so it stays consistent
    // with the lifecycle timestamps rather than being a separate invented value.
    const lastTouchedHoursAgo = Math.min(
      seed.detectedHoursAgo,
      seed.acknowledgedHoursAgo ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
      seed.resolvedHoursAgo ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
    );

    return {
      id: seed.id,
      siteId: seed.siteId,
      assetId: seed.assetId,
      type: seed.type,
      severity: seed.severity,
      status: seed.status,
      title: seed.title,
      description: seed.description,
      metrics: seed.metrics,
      detectedAt: at(seed.detectedHoursAgo),
      updatedAt: at(lastTouchedHoursAgo),
      acknowledgedAt: seed.acknowledgedHoursAgo === null ? null : at(seed.acknowledgedHoursAgo),
      resolvedAt: seed.resolvedHoursAgo === null ? null : at(seed.resolvedHoursAgo),
      assignee: seed.assignee,
      source: seed.source,
      version: 0,
    };
  });

  return { sites: SITES, alerts, notes: NOTE_SEEDS };
}

/** Exposed for the seeding routine, which needs the lifecycle timings to write audit events. */
export const ALERT_LIFECYCLE = ALERT_SEEDS.map((seed) => ({
  id: seed.id,
  detectedHoursAgo: seed.detectedHoursAgo,
  acknowledgedHoursAgo: seed.acknowledgedHoursAgo,
  resolvedHoursAgo: seed.resolvedHoursAgo,
  status: seed.status,
  assignee: seed.assignee,
}));

export function buildSeedData(now: Date): SeedData {
  const at = (hoursAgo: number): string =>
    new Date(now.getTime() - hoursAgo * 3_600_000).toISOString();

  const alerts: Alert[] = ALERT_SEEDS.map((seed) => {
    // `updated_at` is the most recent thing that happened to the alert, so it stays consistent
    // with the lifecycle timestamps rather than being a separate invented value.
    const lastTouchedHoursAgo = Math.min(
      seed.detectedHoursAgo,
      seed.acknowledgedHoursAgo ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
      seed.resolvedHoursAgo ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
    );

    return {
      id: seed.id,
      siteId: seed.siteId,
      assetId: seed.assetId,
      type: seed.type,
      severity: seed.severity,
      status: seed.status,
      title: seed.title,
      description: seed.description,
      metrics: seed.metrics,
      detectedAt: at(seed.detectedHoursAgo),
      updatedAt: at(lastTouchedHoursAgo),
      acknowledgedAt: seed.acknowledgedHoursAgo === null ? null : at(seed.acknowledgedHoursAgo),
      resolvedAt: seed.resolvedHoursAgo === null ? null : at(seed.resolvedHoursAgo),
      assignee: seed.assignee,
      source: seed.source,
      version: 0,
    };
  });

  return { sites: SITES, alerts, notes: NOTE_SEEDS };
}

/** Exposed for the seeding routine, which needs the lifecycle timings to write audit events. */
export const ALERT_LIFECYCLE = ALERT_SEEDS.map((seed) => ({
  id: seed.id,
  detectedHoursAgo: seed.detectedHoursAgo,
  acknowledgedHoursAgo: seed.acknowledgedHoursAgo,
  resolvedHoursAgo: seed.resolvedHoursAgo,
  status: seed.status,
  assignee: seed.assignee,
}));

git add -A && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Add REST API and the AI insight service with guardrails

API
- Express 5 app factory (no listen) so supertest drives the real app
- Filtering, ranking, faceting and pagination as pure functions over a loaded
  board; facets exclude their own dimension so a chip shows what selecting it
  would give, and sorting always tie-breaks by id so pages cannot duplicate rows
- Optimistic concurrency: the version guard lives in the UPDATE's WHERE clause,
  so read-compare-write is atomic at the database rather than in app code
- Consistent error envelope with a request id; 400/404/409/422/413/429 each have
  a specific meaning and body-parser failures no longer surface as 500s

AI feature
- Ollama backend driven by the same Zod schema twice: converted to JSON Schema
  as a structured-output constraint, then used again to validate the reply
- Guardrails: schema validation with one repair round-trip, groundedness
  (every figure must trace to what the model was shown), foreign-site detection
  (fatal), prompt-injection containment, and a priority cross-check that shows
  both verdicts rather than silently picking one
- The deterministic engine is fallback, independent baseline and test substrate;
  it never sees the model's output and the model never sees its playbooks
- Degraded answers are excluded from the cache, so a fallback produced while
  Ollama was down cannot pin an alert to the playbook answer forever
- POST /insight never fails because the AI failed: absent, unreachable, slow,
  verbose, malformed and wrong-site all end in a usable 200 with an honest label

124 tests passing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline | head -2

input.prompt:
You are adding an **AI evaluation harness** to an existing, working full-stack TypeScript monorepo at /Users/qingfengrumeng/Desktop/AlertSystem. The app is a "Renewable Operations Incident Board" for solar/battery sites. It has an AI-assisted feature that summarises an alert, suggests a priority, and proposes next actions.

**Read the existing code first — you must match its architecture, naming and comment style.** Start with these files:
- `apps/api/src/ai/` — `types.ts`, `prompt.ts`, `guards.ts`, `rule-engine.ts`, `ollama.client.ts`, `insight.service.ts`
- `apps/api/src/domain/triage.ts` and `playbooks.ts`
- `apps/api/src/db/seed-data.ts` — the 18 seeded alerts and 6 sites
- `packages/shared/src/insight.ts` — `ModelInsightSchema`, `InsightPayloadSchema`, `normaliseInsight`
- `apps/api/src/testing/test-db.ts` — how a seeded in-memory DB is created

## Context you need

- The `ModelClient` seam (apps/api/src/ai/types.ts) is what talks to Ollama. `createOllamaClient({baseUrl, model})` returns one. Default model `llama3.2:3b`, base URL `http://127.0.0.1:11434`.
- `runGuards(...)` in `guards.ts` returns `{warnings, fatal, confidence, disagreement}`. `checkGroundedness`, `checkSiteReferences`, `detectInjection`, `assessDisagreement` are individually exported.
- `parseModelOutput(raw)` is exported from `apps/api/src/ai/insight.service.ts` and returns `{ok:true,value}` or `{ok:false,problem}`.
- `ruleBasedInsight(context)` in `rule-engine.ts` is the deterministic baseline.
- `AlertContext` = `{alert, site, triage, recentNotes}`.
- `computeTriage(input, {now, portfolioMaxCapacityMw})` from `domain/triage.ts`.
- The api package script `eval` already exists: `"eval": "tsx eval/run-eval.ts"`. So your entry point must be `apps/api/eval/run-eval.ts`.
- ESM + NodeNext: **relative imports must carry the `.js` extension** (e.g. `import { x } from '../src/ai/guards.js'`). TypeScript is strict with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `verbatimModuleSyntax` — use `import type` for types.
- **Ollama is NOT installed on this machine.** Your harness must therefore run and produce a useful report even with no model reachable, and must say clearly that model-dependent metrics could not be measured. Do not attempt to install Ollama.

## What to build

**`apps/api/eval/golden-set.ts`** — a labelled evaluation set of ~20 cases. Build it from the seeded alerts (import `buildSeedData` / use a seeded in-memory DB via the existing test helper so the alerts are the real ones), plus a handful of extra hand-written adversarial cases if useful. Each case carries human labels:
- `expectedPriorityBand`: the priority a competent operator would assign (a single `Priority` or an acceptable set of two adjacent bands — pick one representation and justify it in a comment).
- `expectSafetyFlag`: boolean — whether a competent assessment must flag a safety risk.
- `mustNotClaim`: optional list of strings/numbers that would indicate hallucination for that case.
- a short `rationale` explaining the label, so a reader can disagree with the label rather than guess at it.
Be honest in comments that these labels are your own judgement from ordinary renewable-O&M practice and have not been validated by a domain expert.

**`apps/api/eval/metrics.ts`** — pure, unit-testable scoring functions:
- `schemaValidityRate` — fraction of raw model responses that parse into `ModelInsightSchema` (count repairs separately).
- `groundednessViolationRate` — fraction of answers where `checkGroundedness` produced a warning.
- `priorityAgreement` — exact-band agreement and within-one-band agreement, model vs the human label, AND model vs the deterministic rules. Report all three; they answer different questions.
- `safetyRecall` — of the cases labelled `expectSafetyFlag: true`, how many the answer flagged. Also report false-positive rate on the others.
- `foreignSiteRate` — fraction where `checkSiteReferences` returned fatal.
Keep these pure so they can be tested without a model.

**`apps/api/eval/run-eval.ts`** — the runner. It must:
- Accept flags: `--model <name>`, `--base-url <url>`, `--json` (machine-readable output), `--limit <n>`, `--baseline` (score the deterministic engine instead of the model — this is a genuinely useful control: it shows what the numbers look like with no model at all).
- Check model availability first (`client.isAvailable()`), and if unreachable, print a clear message explaining that model metrics cannot be measured, then still run and report the `--baseline` numbers so the harness always produces something.
- Run each case, collect raw responses, apply the same parse/normalise/guard pipeline the production service uses (reuse the exported functions — do NOT reimplement them, that would defeat the purpose).
- Print a readable table to stdout with all metrics, plus a per-case breakdown of failures.
- Write a JSON report to `apps/api/eval/results/latest.json` (this path is already in .gitignore).
- Exit non-zero **only** on harness errors, not on poor scores — this is a measurement tool, not a gate. Explain that choice in a comment.
